exposure: Length of second stage of labor (0-179 min (NSS), 180-299 min (PSS), and ≥300 min (EPSS))
outcome: Neonatal morbidities (CPAP use, birth weight, composite neonatal outcomes)
cohort: Nulliparous women with singleton gestations and cephalic presentation who reached 10 cm of cervical dilation at gestational age 36 0/7-41 6/7 (n = 661)
finding: While the majority of nulliparous women delivered vaginally, women with epidural anesthesia and an extremely prolonged second stage of labor (≥300 min) had significantly higher rates of postpartum hemorrhage, third-degree lacerations, and adverse neonatal outcomes.
birth_weight: Neonatal birth weight was significantly higher in the extremely prolonged second stage group compared to the normal second stage group.
